---
name: lapis-markdown
description: Create and edit rich Lapis/Mira Markdown, including grid tables, directives, extended task states, properties, links and embeds.
---

# Lapis Markdown

Lapis/Mira supports a richer authoring surface than the common Obsidian-compatible
subset: grid tables with spans, directives, list callouts, extended task states,
code-line metadata, math, diagrams and rich editable previews. Use the Lapis
contract rather than limiting a note to upstream examples. Load detail by task:

- [Rich syntax and examples](references/RICH_SYNTAX.md): grid tables, directives, code, math and diagrams.
- [Properties and links](references/PROPERTIES_AND_LINKS.md): typed data, file identity and metadata.
- [Callouts and task states](references/CALLOUTS_AND_TASKS.md): folding, list callouts and nonbinary markers.
- [Embeds and previews](references/EMBEDS.md): source ownership, providers and editable hover cards.
- [Editor capabilities](references/EDITOR_CAPABILITIES.md): supported modes, settings defaults, optional AI and doodle dividers.

Read the existing note and nearby vault conventions before editing. Preserve
unrelated frontmatter and document content. Use ordinary Markdown plus Lapis
links and embeds; do not assume every Obsidian extension or plugin is present.

```markdown
---
title: Project Alpha
tags:
  - project/active
aliases:
  - Alpha
status: active
---

# Project Alpha

See [[Project Brief|the brief]] and [[Meeting#Decisions]].

> [!note] Next step
> Review the project plan.

- [ ] Prepare a draft

![[Architecture.png|600]]
```

Use `[[Note]]`, `[[Note|Label]]`, `[[Note#Heading]]`, and
`[[Note#^block-id]]` for internal references. Add `^block-id` to the target
block when creating a block reference. Escape alias pipes inside Markdown
tables. Use vault-relative paths where names are ambiguous.

Embeds prefix a supported internal reference with `!`. Confirm the target
exists and the owning file-type plugin is available. Keep image dimensions
optional. Use standard `[label](https://example.com)` for external links.

Frontmatter must remain valid YAML at the start of the document. Preserve
property types: arrays remain arrays, booleans remain booleans, and quoted
text stays text. Do not replace an entire properties block to change one key.

Check headings, fenced code blocks, YAML and link targets after editing.
When using the CLI, discover its current capabilities with `lapis help` and
the selected host; do not invent Obsidian commands for Lapis. Use application
rename/move facilities when available so internal links can be maintained.

Adapted for Lapis from [Obsidian skills](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills).
See [upstream license](LICENSE.txt).
files.references/CALLOUTS_AND_TASKS.md:
# Lapis callouts, list callouts and task states

Read this for structured emphasis and task markers. These remain Markdown text;
no plugin-private JSON is needed to author them.

## Block callouts

```markdown
> [!note] Decision
> Preserve the rationale alongside the action.

> [!warning]- Collapsed details
> Hidden initially, expandable in rendered views.

> [!tip]+ Expanded details
> Expanded initially, with a collapse control.
```

A plain callout has no folding marker. Minus starts collapsed and plus starts
expanded. Common types include note, info, todo, tip, important, warning, danger,
error, success, failure, question, example, quote and abstract. Supported aliases
include summary/tldr, hint, check/done, faq/help, caution/attention, fail/missing
and cite. Unknown types retain their type and fall back to a generic icon;
a custom visual still depends on the installed renderer/extension.

Nested callouts use nested blockquote prefixes. Keep the inner content quoted
and preserve blank quoted lines when they separate paragraphs.

## Lapis list callouts

List callouts highlight an individual list item without converting the whole
item into a blockquote. Default markers include & for highlighting, @ for
documentation and ? for a question:

```markdown
- & Important context for this item.
- @ Documentation to read before proceeding.
- ? Which option should we choose?
```

Markers require whitespace after the list prefix and after the marker. Catalogs
are extensible: an installed Mira extension may add, replace or disable markers.
Do not assume a custom marker seen in one vault has the same meaning elsewhere.

## Extended task states

```markdown
- [ ] Draft the plan
- [/] Work in progress
- [?] Decide the approach
- [-] Cancelled action
- [!] Important action
- [x] Completed action
```

Lapis/Mira renders a richer state catalog than a binary checkbox. Additional
markers include > (forwarded), < (scheduled), l (location), \* (starred), i
(information), S (savings), I (idea), f (fire), k (key), u/d (trending up/down),
w (win), p/c (thumbs up/down), b (bookmark) and a double quote (quote). Uppercase
X is normalized as complete. Markers are case-sensitive otherwise: i and I,
for example, mean different states.

These are display/task-state markers. A scheduled-looking marker does not itself
create a native scheduled Task or reminder. Native Tasks operations, recurrence
and write authority belong to the Tasks plugin and its discovered CLI/API
contract. Preserve existing task metadata rather than inferring new dates or
rewriting every non-complete marker as an unchecked box.
files.references/EDITOR_CAPABILITIES.md:
# Lapis editor capabilities and defaults

Read this when the user asks for editor behavior, a rich authoring feature or a
feature that appears unavailable. Syntax support and a visible authoring control
are different concerns. A note need not flatten its rich syntax to match a hidden
toolbar. Preserve existing configuration unless changing it is requested.

## Modes and richer authoring

Lapis exposes Source, Live Preview and Reading. Portable Mira also has a split
mode, but Lapis Markdown disables that mode; do not advertise it as a Lapis view.
The complete Mira authoring stack supplies slash commands, formatting, tables,
grid tables, images, math, links, block controls and extension contributions.

Twenty feature descriptors govern mode switch, formatting, headings, lists,
links, tables, grid tables, Mermaid, code, math, frontmatter, images, embeds,
wikilinks, tags, slash commands, block controls, Source, Live Preview and Reading.
They are enabled by default and configured under markdown.mira.features.<feature>.
Use the actual Settings feature name rather than inventing a property spelling.

## Dedicated options

| Setting key                                   | Default | Effect                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| markdown.mira.editor.toolbar.enabled          | false   | Top authoring toolbar in editable surfaces                    |
| markdown.mira.editor.selectionToolbar.enabled | true    | Actions for selected editable text                            |
| markdown.mira.editor.blockToolbar.enabled     | false   | Optional block-type control                                   |
| markdown.mira.editor.doodleDividers.enabled   | false   | Seeded hand-drawn horizontal rules                            |
| markdown.mira.plugins.mermaid.enabled         | true    | Installed Mermaid extension, also subject to its feature flag |
| markdown.mira.plugins.ai.enabled              | false   | Optional AI extension, requiring a configured provider        |
| markdown.mira.frontmatter.defaultOpen         | false   | Initially expanded properties                                 |
| markdown.mira.features.outline-navigation     | true    | Floating Reading outline                                      |

The superseded markdown.mira.features.toolbar key is not the current toolbar
setting. AI availability is not implied by syntax support or an installed skill.

## Doodle dividers and extension metadata

A seeded divider pairs an HTML comment with a horizontal rule:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
<!-- mira-divider:v1:1234abcd -->
---
```

The v1 seed is eight hexadecimal digits. The dedicated setting controls its
rendered authoring behavior; preserve the seed/comment when making unrelated
edits. Without that feature, the underlying horizontal rule remains Markdown.

Registered Lapis Markdown extensions can contribute renderer behavior, actions,
list-callout catalogs and styles through the owning App/surface lifecycle. Do
not treat an arbitrary directive name or copied CSS selector as a portable
capability. Check installed extensions and the actual Source/Live Preview/Reading
result when a document relies on one.

# Lapis embeds and editable previews

Read this for embedded notes, media, plugin-owned documents and preview behavior.

```markdown
![[Projects/Plan]]
![[Projects/Plan#Decisions]]
![[Architecture.png|600]]
![[Architecture.png|600x320]]
![External diagram](https://example.com/diagram.png)
```

Resolve internal targets against the current note's source path and vault.
Check the actual target rather than manufacturing an empty note to satisfy an
embed. Preserve heading/block subpaths and existing size hints when unrelated
to the requested change. An embed is a view of the source, not a duplicate file.

## Provider-owned content

Lapis delegates file previews to the owning installed provider. Markdown notes
and supported images can render through the Markdown surface; audio, video,
PDF, Canvas and Bases behavior depends on the corresponding media/file plugin
and its advertised capability. Do not infer that arbitrary extensions or an
Obsidian community embed work in Lapis. Do not add speculative page/fragment
parameters without checking that provider's actual contract.

A Canvas embedded in Markdown follows the original .canvas source and remains
a read-only projection. A Base embeds a query/view over existing notes. Edit
the underlying source document or note rather than overwriting a derived view.

## Lapis rich note previews

Ordinary internal-link previews and Backlinks/Outgoing Links result previews can
enter the real note editor through Lapis's vault-backed Mira adapter. Their
edits persist to the target note and protect an already dirty editor. This is
application behavior; it is not a new Markdown embed delimiter.

Direct document embeds remain read-only. Do not assume that every visible card
is editable because a hover preview elsewhere supports editing. When using a
preview to edit, wait for persistence before dismissal; a failed save should
remain recoverable. When editing files programmatically, preserve unrelated
content in both the source note and the note containing the embed.

# Lapis properties and links

Read this for property edits, file identity, links and metadata indexing.

## Typed frontmatter

Frontmatter is YAML at the beginning of a note. Lapis indexes it and exposes
property types through its property manager. Change the requested keys while
preserving unrelated values, comments where possible, and scalar/list types.
Use the application property controls when an edit needs a property-type change.

```markdown
---
title: Project Alpha
tags:
  - project/active
aliases:
  - Alpha
status: active
estimate: 3
approved: false
reviewDate: "2026-11-15"
---

# Project Alpha

Review [[Projects/Brief|the brief]] and [[Meeting#Decisions]].

A decision can have a stable block reference. ^decision-one
```

Quote a value when it must remain text rather than a YAML Boolean, number or
timestamp. An absent property, an empty string, false and zero are distinct data.
Tags and aliases are normally lists; do not replace a list with comma-separated
text. Date formatting must match the intended Lapis property type.

## Vault references

| Intent        | Syntax                           |
| ------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Note          | [[Projects/Brief]]               |
| Display label | [[Projects/Brief\|the brief]]    |
| Heading       | [[Meeting#Decisions]]            |
| Block         | [[Meeting#^decision-one]]        |
| External URL  | [reference](https://example.com) |

The backslash above protects a table's alias pipe; outside a Markdown table use
[[Projects/Brief|the brief]]. Use a real note path when names are ambiguous.
Aliases are metadata and suggestions, not a reason to replace the actual target
path with arbitrary display text. Preserve existing stable block IDs.

Lapis resolves targets relative to the owning note and vault. Renames/moves
should use application facilities when available so link maintenance can run.
Do not rewrite unrelated links merely to impose a different path convention.

## Lapis metadata and panels

Headings, links, tags and frontmatter feed Lapis metadata and movable panels.
The note text remains authoritative; panel results and index rows are derived.
Changing a database-looking Base row normally changes the source note property,
not an independent table record. After edits, check the property types and
representative link targets through the actual application.
files.references/RICH_SYNTAX.md:
# Lapis rich Markdown syntax

Read this for Lapis/Mira authoring beyond the common Obsidian-compatible subset.
Lapis includes pipe and grid tables, extended task states, list callouts,
directives, code-line controls, math, Mermaid and rich editable previews. Syntax
and editor controls are separate: see [editor capabilities](EDITOR_CAPABILITIES.md)
for defaults and optional features. Treat the installed Lapis renderer as the
contract rather than limiting a note to upstream Obsidian examples.

## Grid tables and spans

Pipe tables support ordinary alignment markers. Grid tables support explicit
boundaries, multiline cells, sections and spanning cells. Keep border widths
aligned when editing; changing one boundary can alter a span.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
+-------------------+------+
| Table Headings    | Here |
+--------+----------+------+
| Sub    | Headings | Too  |
+========+=================+
| cell   | column spanning |
| spans  +---------:+------+
| rows   |   normal | cell |
+---v----+:---------------:+
|        | cells can be    |
|        | *formatted*     |
|        | **paragraphs**  |
|        | ~~~             |
| multi  | and contain     |
| line   | blocks          |
| cells  | ~~~             |
+========+=========:+======+
| footer |    cells |      |
+--------+----------+------+
```

## Directives

Inline :name[content]{attributes}, leaf ::name[content]{attributes}, and container
:::name forms are parsed. Containers can nest using longer outer colon fences.
A generic directive becomes a portable custom element. An installed extension
can supply its rendering; the syntax does not create a new plugin or component.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
:::mira{title="Decision context"}
Use **Markdown** inside the directive body.
:::
```

## Code blocks with line metadata

Lapis supports highlighted line ranges, optional line numbers, a starting line
number and preserving outer blank lines. Preserve the fence language and metadata
when changing code; directives inside a block are still block content.

`<!-- prettier-ignore -->

````markdown
```ts {2,4-6} showLineNumbers=10 keepOuterBlankLine
const first = 1;
const second = 2;
````

````

nolinenumbers disables numbering for that block. A source-language fence is not
an instruction to execute its content.

## Math and diagrams

Use $E = mc^2$ for inline math and a $$ block for display math. Lapis renders
math through KaTeX; use supported LaTeX, not arbitrary TeX packages. Mermaid is
a registered editor extension and is enabled by default unless settings disable it.

`<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```markdown
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
$$

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Draft --> Review --> Published
```
````

## Other rich content

Footnotes use [^source] and a separate [^source]: definition. Semantic HTML such
as <details>, <summary>, <kbd> and <mark> is supported; raw-HTML policy is
host-controlled. Lapis also renders tags, sized images and extended task markers.
See [callouts and tasks](CALLOUTS_AND_TASKS.md) and [embeds](EMBEDS.md).

Preserve the authoring syntax instead of flattening a rich table, diagram or
callout to plain text. Inspect both Source and Reading/Live Preview when editing
syntax whose layout or renderer matters. Custom extensions may add more
capabilities; do not invent their directive names or configuration.
